name: Can Connect
description: Returns `CRITICAL` if the Agent cannot query the local clstrmgrES cluster manager state (for example, PowerHA is not installed or not running on this node). Returns `OK` otherwise.

name: Cluster Manager Status
description: Returns `OK` if the clstrmgrES cluster manager is in the stable (ST_STABLE) state, `WARNING` if it is in a known transitional state (for example, during a failover event), and `CRITICAL` otherwise (for example, ST_BROKEN or an unrecognized state).

name: Node Status
description: Returns `CRITICAL` if a cluster node reports a CAA state of DOWN in `lscluster -m`, `OK` if it reports UP, and `UNKNOWN` for any other reported state.

name: Resource Group Status
description: Returns `OK` if a resource group is online on at least one node, `WARNING` if it is only in a transitional state (acquiring, releasing, or unmanaged), and `CRITICAL` if it is in the error state or not online anywhere.

name: Application Monitor Status
description: Returns `OK` if an application monitor reports its application ONLINE, `WARNING` if OFFLINE, `CRITICAL` if FAILED, and `UNKNOWN` for any other reported state.

name: CAA Interface Status
description: Returns `CRITICAL` if a CAA network interface reported by `lscluster -m` is DOWN, `OK` if UP, and `UNKNOWN` for any other reported state.

name: CAA SAN Communication Status
description: Returns `WARNING` if the CAA SAN-based communication path to a peer node (`clras sancomm_status`) is DOWN, `OK` otherwise. This is a redundant heartbeat path, so a single node's path being down does not indicate a critical cluster health issue on its own.

name: CAA Disk Communication Status
description: Returns `WARNING` if the CAA disk-based communication path to a peer node (`clras dpcomm_status`) is DOWN, `OK` otherwise. This is a redundant heartbeat path, so a single node's path being down does not indicate a critical cluster health issue on its own.

name: Network Interface Status
description: Returns `CRITICAL` if a PowerHA-monitored network interface reported by `netstat -i` is DOWN, `OK` if UP, and `UNKNOWN` for any other reported state.

name: Volume Group Status
description: Returns `CRITICAL` if any physical volume in a shared volume group is not in the active state, `OK` otherwise.
